name: Disable Account Emails
description: Lets administrators selectively disable specific automated user-account emails sent by Drupal core's user module.
project_description:
The Disable Account Emails module provides site administrators with fine-grained control over which automated user account emails are sent from your Drupal site. This lightweight utility allows you to selectively disable specific types of user-related emails while keeping others active.

How it works: the module leverages Drupal's form and mail alteration hooks. It uses hook_form_FORM_ID_alter() to inject a set of checkboxes into the core Account settings form (entity.user.admin_form) inside a dedicated "Disable Account Emails" details fieldset. It implements hook_mail_alter() to intercept outgoing emails whose module is 'user', and for any email key marked disabled in configuration it sets $message['send'] = FALSE so the email is not delivered. Settings live in the disable_account_emails.settings config object, backed by a config schema, and hook_uninstall() removes that configuration on uninstall.

The module covers nine core user email types (welcome/registration variants, account activation, blocked, cancellation confirmation, deleted, and password recovery) without any code changes. It defines no routes, permissions, services, or plugins of its own; the checkbox UI reuses the core Account settings page, which is already gated by the core 'administer account settings' permission.
